derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Citation statuses observe source_status_ceiling. EN 17007 SER is the spine. ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.3 is the control, not a lifecycle stage - contractors attach to the work sequence rather than sitting inside it. BPMN artifacts are one per group.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: EN 13269:2016 is cited by title only for contract preparation. Its body is paywalled and is not paraphrased into package content, rate tables or acceptance tests.
No standard specifies work-package content (pack D-bis). 7 CFR 1724.53(b)(1) is RUS only. 16.2.3 issues the package; content remains judgment aside from 1910.269(a)(3) hazard transfer.
cl. 4.2 has no contractor, document or procurement component. The register sits on MAI, crews and credentials on HR, awards on SCHD, progress on FRD, pay on FIN.

APQC PCF Utilities has no contractor-management process in categories 10 and 14. Cross-industry 4.2.4 Manage suppliers is manufacturing supply chain, not field-crew contracting. The assignment pack's APQC rows are empty; that is a real finding, not a missed mapping.
NERC CIP-013 is in the pack for this category but is bulk-power cyber. 16 U.S.C. 824o keeps it off local distribution. Named only as a transmission-scoped access variant at 16.5.1.
No pack standard specifies contractor completion-evidence content, progress codes, scorecards, or interface-exception handling. SER.3/SER.4/DTA.1 are the closest names.
16.2.1 uses deliveryRoute, the shared DMN variable with 1.3.4. 3.2.3 commits the roster split; 16.2.1 decides the work item. Three processes, one determination.
16.5.3 and 16.3.1/16.3.2 look like duplicates. They are not: 16.5 is the message, 16.3 is the management. Same split as 13.7 versus 13.4.
13.7.1 qualifies goods suppliers (SPP.5). 16.1 qualifies field contractors (SER.1). Paying them is 13.4.4 versus 16.4.3. Easy to merge; wrong.
ISO 9001:2015 cl. 8.4 is cited by title as the management-system analogue for externally provided processes. Wording from third-party reproductions is not used.

merge_corrections.what: ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.3 was cited with ISO 9001's wording. The clause number is right; its title is Outsourcing. 'Control of externally provided processes, products and services' is ISO 9001:2015 cl. 8.4. A status of clause-verified asserts the clause number AND its title, so a borrowed title is an unearned status.
citation form: a status may not claim more than the citation string supports. 'clause-verified' without a clause dropped to 'consensus'; an asserted absence dropped to 'judgment'.

vocabulary.json is this project's own artifact, not a source. Citing it at 'verified' makes the reference evidence for itself; the cross-process note it carries is a judgment. And 16.4.4's notation.why said 'standing score' where the work is a determination - same correction as 13.7.7, same reason: it is SPEC because no source states the rule, not because it has no instance.
